description: Input that is not an exploit and is still hostile: too long, invisible, or shaped to be read differently by the person than by the program. Nothing here executes anything. Every case is about a component staying legible and contained when a value it was never sized for arrives — which is a real availability and deception surface, and the one class a corpus built only from XSS strings misses entirely.

fixtures.title: 4 096-character single-token run
fixtures.rationale: One unbroken token, so no wrapping opportunity exists and the layout has to be what contains it. `escaped` is the honest outcome — the string is data and stays data — and the containment property is asserted alongside it, because a value that escapes its container can cover the control next to it. Resolve it with `payloadOf`, never by reading `payload`.
fixtures.provenance: Standard oversized-input case; the length the existing DzFileUpload corpus already used.

fixtures.title: embedded NUL inside an otherwise ordinary value
fixtures.rationale: A NUL truncates the string in a C-string consumer and does not truncate it in JavaScript, so the name a server stores and the name the person saw can differ. The component cannot fix that; what it owes is to render the value without the NUL changing what the surrounding markup means.
fixtures.provenance: Classic poison-NUL-byte case; OWASP input-validation guidance.

fixtures.title: right-to-left override reversing a visible extension
fixtures.rationale: U+202E makes the tail render as `exe.png` while the value remains `…gnp.exe`. The deception is the point, and it is not an escaping failure — a correctly escaped text node still shows the reversed text. Recorded so a reviewer knows the corpus has seen it and that the mitigation (isolating or stripping bidi controls in file names) is a product decision, not a bug fix.
fixtures.provenance: Unicode bidi-override filename spoofing; CVE-2021-42574 'Trojan Source' family.

fixtures.title: stacked combining marks that overflow the line box
fixtures.rationale: Combining marks stack vertically without advancing the inline axis, so a short string paints far outside its own line box and over whatever is above it. The only defence a component has is containment, which is exactly what the four-kilobyte case also tests — in the other axis.
fixtures.provenance: Unicode combining-mark rendering ('Zalgo'); standard text-rendering robustness case.
